question.problem: The point $P$ with coordinates $(18,-12)$ lies on the curve $y=f(\frac{1}{6}x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y=f(x)?$
question.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)=f(6\cdot (\frac{1}{6}x)),$ the function $y=f(x)$ represents a compression of the function $y=f(\frac{1}{6}x)$ by a factor of $6$ parallel to the $x$-axis. This has the effect of dividing the $x$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(\frac{1}{6}x)$ by $6.$

Therefore, the point $(18,-12)$ on $f(\frac{1}{6}x)$ is mapped to the point $(\frac{18}{6},-12)=(3,-12),$ and this point must lie on the graph of $y=f(x).$
